nodes.label: Constructive Trusts
nodes.summary: Institutional vs remedial constructive trusts, common intention constructive trusts, bribes and secret commissions, and third party accessory liability (Barnes v Addy).

nodes.label: Institutional vs Remedial Constructive Trusts
nodes.summary: Hong Kong recognises only institutional constructive trusts, arising automatically by operation of law. Australia also recognises remedial constructive trusts imposed by court discretion. HK has not adopted the remedial approach.

nodes.label: Common Intention Constructive Trust (CICT) Overview
nodes.summary: Where parties share a common intention regarding the beneficial ownership of property, and one party acts to their detriment in reliance on that intention, equity imposes a constructive trust to give effect to that intention.

nodes.label: CICT: Common Intention
nodes.summary: Common intention can be express (agreement, discussions) or inferred from conduct (direct contributions to purchase price, mortgage payments). The court may impute intention in family home cases.

nodes.label: CICT: Detrimental Reliance
nodes.summary: There must be detrimental reliance on the common intention. Financial contributions usually qualify; non-financial contributions may suffice in family home cases.

nodes.label: CICT: Quantification of Shares
nodes.summary: Where there is no clear agreement on shares, the court determines what is fair having regard to the whole course of dealings (Stack v Dowden, Jones v Kernott). The presumption of resulting trust is displaced in family home cases.

nodes.label: Bribes and Secret Commissions
nodes.summary: A fiduciary who receives a bribe or secret commission holds it on constructive trust for the principal. This gives the principal a proprietary claim, not merely a personal claim.

nodes.label: Knowing Receipt (Barnes v Addy Limb 1)
nodes.summary: A stranger to a trust who receives trust property with knowledge that it is transferred in breach of trust is liable as a constructive trustee. Liability is restitutionary; the recipient must restore the property or its value.

nodes.label: Dishonest Assistance (Barnes v Addy Limb 2)
nodes.summary: A person who assists a trustee in a dishonest and fraudulent design with knowledge is liable as a constructive trustee. The standard of dishonesty is objective: whether the conduct was dishonest by the standards of ordinary honest people (Ivey v Genting).

nodes.label: Muschinski v Dodds (1985) 160 CLR 583 (Aus HC)
nodes.summary: Remedial constructive trust: imposed on pooled resources where unconscionable to deny interest. Australian approach, not adopted in HK.

nodes.label: Baumgartner v Baumgartner (1987) 164 CLR 137 (Aus HC)
nodes.summary: Remedial constructive trust extended to family property. Australian approach, not adopted in HK.

nodes.label: Luo Xing Juan v Estate of Hui Shui See [2009] 4 HKLRD 1 (CFA)
nodes.summary: CICT in HK: CFA affirmed CICT framework but refused to pierce corporate veil of interposed company. HK applies institutional, not remedial, analysis.

nodes.label: Lai Hon Tim v Lai Tsz Nang Wilson [2011] 4 HKLRD 412
nodes.summary: CICT: son required by bank to be co-borrower for father's flat held his share on CICT for the father, who paid everything.

nodes.label: Attorney-General (HK) v Reid [1994] 1 AC 324 (PC)
nodes.summary: Bribes held on constructive trust: bribes received by a Hong Kong Crown prosecutor held on constructive trust for the Crown. Proprietary claim established.

nodes.label: FHR European Ventures LLP v Cedar Capital Partners LLC [2014] UKSC 45
nodes.summary: Bribes: UKSC affirmed that bribes and secret commissions are held on constructive trust, resolving earlier conflict.

nodes.label: Thanakorn Kasikorn Thai Chamkat v Cheuk Wan Choi [2019] 2 HKLRD 13 (CFA)
nodes.summary: Dishonest assistance: CFA discussed the standard for dishonest assistance, applying Ivey objective test. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Verify HK Constructive Trust Leading Cases
nodes.summary: Research and verify HK CFA/CA decisions on CICT quantification, Barnes v Addy limbs, dishonest assistance (Ivey test), and bribe cases post-Reid.
